title: MitoMatch: AlphaFold-Multimer Prediction of Mitochondrial Protein Interaction Networks
author: Tibi Puiu reporting on Nature Communications study
key_claims: AlphaFold-Multimer adapted to screen 630,003 possible protein pairs across human mitochondrial proteome (~1,123 proteins)
2,895 high-confidence interactions predicted at ~85% precision threshold; 57% were absent from six major interaction databases
85 previously uncharacterized mitochondrial proteins assigned potential partners and functional hypotheses
COA4-COX11 binding predicted by MitoMatch and validated experimentally in yeast and human cells; COA4 deletion reduces COX11 levels, mitochondrial copper, and respiratory complex IV abundance
methodology: AlphaFold-Multimer complex prediction; threshold calibration against 1,338 known positives and 15,000 known negatives; experimental validation via co-immunoprecipitation and gene deletion in human cell lines
key_risk: Computational predictions require experimental confirmation at scale; false positives remain possible outside the calibrated mitochondrial compartment where encounter probability is higher
next_experiment: Expand to whole-proteome screening with evolutionary co-conservation filtering (cf. Predictomes 2025); integrate with C9 neuromorphic protein-interaction graph for active-inference modeling of metabolic networks
notes: Excellent example of L1 AI-driven biology. The 'structure-to-function' pipeline parallels C9's own 'data-to-insight' Assembly Index workflow. Cross-species conservation analysis (11 organisms) adds evolutionary robustness.
